Printed invoice numbers use the format `INV-<4-digit year of issue>-<sequence zero-padded to 6 digits>`, e.g. `INV-2026-000123`.

**Why:** The accounting export sorts invoice numbers as text, so the zero-padding is required for correct ordering (without it, `INV-2026-10` would sort before `INV-2026-9`).

**How to apply:** Any code that generates, formats, parses or validates invoice numbers must follow this exact format: literal `INV`, hyphen, 4-digit issue year, hyphen, 6-digit zero-padded sequence. Decided 2026-11-26; no code change was made at that time.

content.text:
I added `formatInvoiceNumber(year, sequence)` to `lib/invoices.js` and exported it. It returns numbers in the `INV-YYYY-NNNNNN` format with the sequence zero-padded to 6 digits, for example `INV-2026-000123`. That's the format recorded in project memory, which exists because the accounting export sorts the numbers as text.

All 8 existing tests pass, and calling `formatInvoiceNumber(2026, 123)` returned `INV-2026-000123`.

I didn't add a test for the new function, and I didn't wire it into `createInvoice`. Invoices still get ids like `inv_3`.
